transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess I may have gotten a little carried away with a project at the historical society. I thought I could manage the whole fundraiser myself, and I started making quilt designs, calling volunteers, putting together schedules… promising things by deadlines that, looking back, probably weren’t very realistic. I was trying to be helpful, you know? But it’s gotten a bit much, and I thought maybe I should come talk to someone.
Have you noticed times when your mood or energy level has been significantly elevated, such that you felt unusually confident, energetic, or required less sleep to feel rested?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic, but at first I felt almost… glowing, like every idea I had was just wonderful and I could really make it all work. It felt good, honestly.

But then if someone questioned me or slowed me down, I’d get snappish. Not proud of that. I acted like they were standing in my way, even if they were probably just trying to help. Does that make sense?
How long did you feel that way—glowing and unusually confident and energetic? Was it just for a few days or longer?

It was… longer than just a few days. I suppose I kept telling myself it was just being enthusiastic, but that overdriven period with the historical society went on for about five months before it all kind of fell apart. I know that probably sounds like a lot.

During that five-month period, did you ever feel so full of energy or so powerful that it felt different from your usual self, almost like you were on top of the world—or did it feel more like constant stress and pressure to keep up with everything you were doing?

I’d like to say it was just stress, because that sounds more reasonable, doesn’t it? But… no, it wasn’t only that.

At the time I really did feel like I’d found something important. I truly believed my heritage quilt ideas were going to put our little town on the map, like this was finally the thing only I could make happen. I know that sounds a bit grand now, but it felt very real then.
Was there a specific time when your mood was so high or your energy was so intense that it was clearly different from your usual self, even before the project started to fall apart?

Yes… I think there was. Early on, before things got messy, I felt almost glowing, like every idea I had was a good one—wonderful, even. I don’t usually feel that certain about myself.

And I tried to keep it pleasant, but if anyone questioned me, I got… snappish. I’d act like they were standing in my way, even when they probably weren’t. I’m not proud of that, but yes, it was different from my usual self.
Can you think back to when you first started feeling so confident and energized—was there a clear beginning to that mood, or did it gradually build up alongside the stress of the project?

I think it did have a beginning, yes… not all at once like a switch, but early on I remember feeling almost glowing, like everything I thought of was somehow a wonderful idea. It didn’t just feel like pressure yet.

I probably made it sound nicer to myself at the time—enthusiasm, purpose, that sort of thing. But if someone questioned me, I’d get snappish, more than I should have, and I’d feel like they were getting in the way. I don’t like saying that, but that’s how it was.
Can you think of a specific week or even a few days when you clearly felt more energetic or confident than usual, even before any of the project-related stress really started to build up?

Yes… I think there were a few days right near the beginning when it felt very clear. I don’t want to overstate it, but I felt almost glowing, like every idea I had was wonderful.

And before the pressure really piled on, I was already… more certain than I usually am. If someone questioned me, I’d get snappish, like they were standing in the way. I know that doesn’t sound very nice, but that’s how it felt then.

Can you recall if there was a distinct period—like a few days or more—where your mood was unusually high and your energy was abnormally elevated, clearly separate from just being excited or stressed about the project?

Yes… I think there was a distinct stretch, more than just normal excitement. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but at first I felt almost glowing, like every idea I had was wonderful.

And it wasn’t only enthusiasm. If someone questioned me, I got snappish—like they were standing in my way. I didn’t like that about myself, but yes, it did feel clearly different from my usual self.
Can you estimate how many days in a row you felt that unusually high mood and energy—was it at least four consecutive days, most of the day nearly every day?

At least four days, yes… I mean, if I’m being honest, it was much longer than that.

I sort of told myself it was just being very dedicated to the historical society project, but that overdriven feeling went on for… about five months, I think, before everything really fell apart. I know that sounds like a lot.

Can you confirm if there was a time when you felt unusually high and energized for at least four days in a row, most of the day, nearly every day, separate from just being excited or stressed about the project?

Yes… yes, I can confirm that. It wasn’t just a few good days or being excited, really. That overdriven feeling with the historical society project went on for about five months before everything fell apart.

I know that sounds like a long time, and I maybe tried to make it sound more reasonable at the time, but… yes, it was most of the time, nearly every day.

Can you confirm if there was a distinct period where your mood was unusually high and your energy was abnormally elevated for at least four days in a row, most of the day, nearly every day, separate from just being excited or stressed about the project?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I know I keep trying to explain it as being committed to the project, but it did feel separate from ordinary excitement.

At first I felt almost glowing, like every idea I had was wonderful. And then if anyone questioned me, I’d get snappish—like they were standing in my way. I’m not proud of that, but yes, it was definitely a distinct period where my mood and energy were unusually high.
